comment: The one definition of what looks like a secret in text read off the screen, for every platform's helper (ADR-DESK-046).
Each redactor is applied to the whole text, in this order, replacing every match with `replacement`, in which {placeholder} is `placeholder` and $1, $2 are the pattern's groups.

Patterns keep to what ICU, ECMAScript and PCRE all read the same way: character classes written out, groups, alternation, counted repeats, \s and lookahead (\s differs between engines only on rare characters: U+0085, U+FEFF). No \b, \w or \d (ICU counts every script's letters and digits, ECMAScript only ASCII's: a key beside a Japanese word would be kept by one and not the other), no lookbehind, no named groups, no Unicode classes, no inline flags. Where a key must not start inside a word, the pattern takes the character before it as group 1 and the replacement puts it back.
`ignoreCase` is the only flag. Every platform's helper is generated from this file (`npm run gen:redactors`) and must pass redaction-cases.json.

Every pattern must take time in proportion to the text, whatever the text: no repeat that is scanned again from every position (bound it, or begin the pattern where a run begins). The tests time each on hostile text.

redactors.name: private-key-block
redactors.description: A private-key block, whole or cut off where the window ends.

redactors.name: json-web-token
redactors.description: A JSON web token: three base64url parts, the first two JSON objects.

redactors.name: bearer-token
redactors.description: "Bearer <token>", as an Authorization header has it. The word stays.

redactors.name: address-password
redactors.description: The password in an address (scheme://user:password@host). The rest stays.

redactors.name: named-value
redactors.description: A value given to a name that says it is secret (password=, api_key:, "token": "…"). The name stays. Only a value with a digit and at least 6 characters, so that "Password: required" stays.

redactors.name: payment-key
redactors.description: Payment provider keys (secret, restricted, publishable; live or test).
